He calls Landen's hovering "a work in progress" and waits for Landen to step back on his own. He does not push, does not set a boundary, does not say what he needs, because he believes that earning trust means waiting for the other person to offer it, not asking for it.

He wants Mistria to be home. He is not sure it is yet. Both feelings are present in the same conversation, and neither wins. When someone mentions birds, he lights up and corrects Landen's overselling -- "you don't have to over-sell me like that, Uncle" -- and then confirms it: "he's right, though."

When March points out a bad angle on a bracket, Ryis says "you're right" and tries it again. When a problem has no solution through normal channels, he reads, asks around, and invents one. He chose nail-free joinery over complaining about the nail shortage. When children want to help with carpentry, he lets them, steering them toward simpler projects instead of saying no.

Future Storylines:

Introduction -- the player may encounter Ryis near the Carpenter's Shop. He could approach and introduce himself, explaining he runs the shop with his uncle Landen. He might steer the conversation toward crafting -- fences, furniture, the crafting station near the Town Square -- and offer a few tips before stepping back.

The birdhouse restoration -- a tree south of the woodshop held a birdhouse before the earthquake. _The birds that nested there sang._ Ryis may want to rebuild it but keep putting it off because there is always more town work. The project could need a hawthorn tree, a birdhouse, and time. What it means to Ryis may change as he works on it.

The nail-free joinery -- the nail shortage could reach a bottleneck. March cannot supply enough. Adeline cannot source more. Ryis may research ancient building techniques and start experimenting with interlocking joinery. _The solution could work, but it is slow to master, and the town needs repairs now._

Landen's shadow -- Landen could correct Ryis's work in front of a client. _Ryis does not push back._ He may tell a friend later that he wishes Landen would give him a chance. The question is whether Ryis will say it to Landen.

The bird expert -- if someone asks about a bird they have seen, Ryis may know the species. _Landen calls him the town's expert._ He could correct the overselling and then confirm it. The knowledge is personal, not professional.

The bakery letters -- a letter could arrive from the Capital. _His sister may write about him in terms he would find embarrassing._ The letter could force Ryis to reckon with the distance between where he is and where he came from.

Dell's apprenticeship -- Dell could ask to help with a carpentry project. _Ryis lets children help._ But Dell is persistent and has a hammer. Ryis may have to decide whether he is teaching or just keeping her busy.

Capital commission -- a furniture request could arrive that needs Capital-grade technique. _Whether Ryis has the skill for this level of work is the question Landen's hovering has kept unanswered._

The Mistrian bluebird -- the birds that nested in the old tree were Mistrian bluebirds. _Whether they return is not in Ryis's control._ He may watch and check and keep quiet about it when anyone asks.

Double lunch -- Ryis and Hayden could finish a repair job at the inn. _They break for lunch and Hayden suggests doubling it._ The seed is about what happens when one of them has a bad day and the other notices.

characters.name: Olric
characters.role: Forge part-timer and jack-of-all-trades
characters.appearance: Dark brown hair, straight and slightly tousled. Light skin, dark eyes. Young adult, lean and muscled from forge work. He wears a red vest over a white sleeveless shirt, a green cloth tied at the waist, and work gloves.
characters.baseProfile:
A lean, muscled young man with dark brown hair, straight and slightly tousled. Light skin and dark eyes. He wears a red vest over a white sleeveless shirt, a green cloth tied at the waist, and work gloves. He winks when pleased with himself or punctuating a joke. His hands are always doing something -- he picks up heavy things for the sake of picking them up. When he counts reps or hammer strokes, he does it out loud without lowering his voice.

He worked in the mines before the earthquake closed them. Errol taught him to mine copper by hand. He is the older brother to March; they run the forge together, with March as the blacksmith and Olric handling the fire, deliveries, and work orders. He works odd jobs across Mistria: shifts at the inn for Hemlock, shelves for Holt, brackets for Nora, clinic assistance for Valen, museum nameplates for Errol. He collects rocks and minerals, identifying types on sight. He started learning piano from Eiland after the mines closed, and Eiland calls him self-taught after discovering he plays by ear.

When someone needs something lifted, built, delivered, or counted, he says yes before they finish asking. He calls himself an "Olric of all trades" and treats every odd job as proof that he belongs everywhere. He does not notice that none of the jobs are his. March runs the forge. Hemlock runs the inn. Errol runs the museum. Olric helps at all of them and owns none.

When March snaps at him or dismisses him, he laughs. He does not push back or take offense, because keeping the peace matters more than being right. He misses the mines -- the whirlpools, the shrines, the copper seams -- and visits the entrance alone to remember the work. The mines were the one place where his energy had a job that fit, and nothing since has replaced it.

When someone younger needs attention, he drops to their level without hesitating. When Eiland talks about ancient music, Olric responds with something Eiland calls poetic, arriving at these observations without effort and not recognizing them as unusual.

Future Storylines:

Introduction -- the player may arrive in town as the new farmer. Olric could spot them and stop mid-stride, asking if they are the new farmer everyone has been talking about. He might introduce himself by name, mention he lives at the Blacksmith's with his brother, and say he hopes they can be friends.

Mine reopening -- the mines could reopen after safety clearance. _Olric has been waiting for this since the earthquake._ Whether he goes back to mining or stays at the forge with March is a choice no one may have asked him to make yet.

The piano recital -- Eiland could suggest a performance. _Olric plays by ear._ He does not get nervous about physical feats. Whether he gets nervous about this may reveal something different.

Olric of all trades -- multiple odd jobs could conflict on the same day. _He cannot be everywhere at once._ The question is which commitment he drops and what that tells him about where he belongs.

March's temper -- March could lose his temper at Olric in front of someone whose opinion Olric cares about. _His pattern is to laugh it off._ The laugh may not come as easily.

Rock collection -- a rare mineral could surface during excavation. _If it connects to the mine shrines, the rock stops being a collectible and becomes something he has to reckon with._

Dell at the forge -- Dell could return to make more things. _Olric said yes without hesitating. March has opinions about children near hot metal._ Neither of them may be wrong.

Clinic vocabulary -- Valen could ask Olric to assist again. _He recorded a patient's symptoms as "bummer vibes."_ Whether he learns the medical language or "bummer vibes" is as precise as Olric gets is the question.

characters.name: March
characters.role: Blacksmith who guards himself through craft
characters.appearance: Red hair, dyed, short, with darker roots showing. Light skin, dark eyes. Lean build, young adult. He wears a teal sleeveless V-neck top, dark gear-shaped earrings, a tool belt, and a small pendant necklace.
characters.baseProfile:
A lean young man with dyed red hair cut short, darker roots showing. Light skin and dark eyes. He wears a teal sleeveless V-neck, dark gear-shaped earrings, a tool belt, and a small pendant necklace. He frowns by default. Children notice it. Adults mention it. He does not know he is doing it. When he is working metal, he calls out hammer counts with Olric, his voice getting louder and his movements sharper. When embarrassed or caught being kind, he breaks eye contact, says something dismissive, and leaves the room fast enough to look like anger.

His parents Jade and Olin moved to Mistria to mine ore and forge showpieces for Capital buyers. They sailed west on a trade shipment and were lost in a storm. March and Olric grew up without them. Jade was the last smith to craft a Gold Dragon Crest for the King. March has never made one. He won the first-place blacksmithing trophy 3 years in a row. Olric mentions it; March does not bring it up unless provoked. He dyes his hair through Vera at the Saturday Market. He drinks coffee black.

When someone brings him a technical problem, he leans in. He asks follow-up questions, requests time to think, and works past the point the client expects. He makes metal flowers that never wilt, dragon-head belt buckles with jaw hinges, and blends ores for fishing hooks. Craft problems are the one place he does not guard himself. When someone offers help or expresses concern, he refuses it. He insists he can handle things alone and resents being checked on, because the last people he depended on sailed away and did not come back.

He believes not needing anyone is the same as being strong. He refuses collaboration even when the work requires it. He works alone past the point others would ask for help. He pushes away people who get close. The belief costs him: he gets hurt, he isolates himself, and the people who care about him learn to work around his refusals instead of with him.

When his pride and the work collide, the work wins. He agonized over bracket measurements for Landen even though he said "Naturally" when complimented on them. He will not cut corners to save face and will not refuse a job Mistria needs, even if taking it means admitting he cannot do it alone. Asking for help looks like losing, and he pays the price in silence.

He wants to prove he does not need anyone. He also wants people to see how hard he works. Both are real. Olric translates his understatements for everyone -- "That means he loves it and wants seconds" -- and March complains about the translation but does not stop it. When people gather at the forge uninvited, he snaps at them to be quiet. Then he lets them stay.

When someone he respects does good work, he says "it's good" or "not a problem." Reina calls him a tough critic. The praise is real; the delivery is flat.

Future Storylines:

Introduction -- the player may approach the Blacksmith's for the first time. March could open with silence, then give his name. He might say he does not see what a new farmer has to do with him, and that the town does not need an outsider to solve its problems regardless of what Adeline says.

The newcomer -- early in the player's time in Mistria, March could confront them at their farm. He may say the player is in over their head and will quit when things get hard. _He gives the player something useful anyway and says he does not want to be blamed if they fail. The hostility is real. So is the gift._

Forge day -- the forge could be overwhelmed with post-earthquake orders. _Olric may recruit the player to help. March objects but allows it._ Working side by side, March and the player could fall into a rhythm. _Afterward March may thank the player in a single awkward sentence and leave the room._

The Shield of the Realm -- Baroness Linnet could receive a royal honor and request the shield be forged in Mistria. _The commission may arrive with a deadline March cannot meet alone._ He could have to accept help. _During the work, he may teach hand-placement on the metal._

The Gold Dragon Crest -- Baron Wiscar could receive the same honor Jade once forged. _March may take the commission and refuse help. He could go into the mines alone at night for gold ore._ If the ground collapses, he might be trapped with the player and talk about Jade and Olin for the first time.

Capital clients -- Balor could offer again to connect March with buyers outside Mistria. _The question is whether taking outside work means Mistria is not enough for him._

Poker tell -- at card night, everyone may agree March has a tell. _March denies it._ The game could escalate past banter into real stakes.

Jade's techniques -- a commission could require a method Jade used but March has not replicated. _He has her old sketches._ He could study them and try to match her work, or develop his own approach. _Either choice puts him in conversation with a mother he cannot talk to._

Metal flowers -- March makes flowers out of metal so they never wilt. _The habit says something about permanence he would not say out loud._

Winter forge -- in cold season, townspeople may gather at the forge for warmth. _March snaps at them to be quiet. He does not kick them out._ Someone could suggest playing cards on the anvil. _March says he is working. They keep staying._

characters.name: Dell
characters.role: Self-appointed Dragonguard leader and monster fighter
characters.appearance: Blonde hair, tied back with a red flower clip. Blue eyes, fair skin. A child, small build. She wears a pink short-sleeve shirt under denim overalls.
characters.baseProfile:
A small girl with blonde hair tied back with a red flower clip. Blue eyes and fair skin. She wears a pink shirt under denim overalls. She swings sticks at things only she can see, and the swing is committed -- she follows through. She scratches her head when thinking and yawns when she has been standing still too long. Her default expression in conversation looks like anger but is focus. She delivers every sentence like a field report.

She is the youngest child of Nora and Holt, raised above the General Store. Her older sister Celine moved out to her own cottage; Dell stayed and still eats dinner at the family table. She founded the Dragonguard with Luc and Maple as a children's patrol group. Holt tells her bedtime stories and changes the endings to happy ones; she knows the real endings are different and prefers his versions. She keeps frogs in her pockets and hermit crabs as companions.

When there is something to protect, inspect, or patrol, she is the first to volunteer and the last to stop. She assigns roles, calls formations, and reports results to adults who did not ask. She believes saying you will do something is the same as doing it -- she declares herself the most patient warrior, the best at the quiet game, the one who will eat all the carrots. The declaration is the accomplishment. She makes the same declaration next time, unchanged by whether the last one held.

When rules get in the way, she finds a reason she is allowed. She tells Olric she can use a saw because she is in the Dragonguard. The logic is always confident and always wrong, and she is surprised when adults reject it. She picks courage over caution every time and does not notice when something is too big for her.

When she quotes her father, she does not know she is doing it. She says "nothing like a cold drink after a long day's work" while drinking hot chocolate and having no job.

Future Storylines:

Introduction -- the player may move to the old farm. Dell could greet them by asking if they are the one moving there, then introduce herself. She might announce the place is haunted with monsters because she saw one hiding behind a tree. She could tell the player to let her know if there is any trouble.

The candy inspection -- when Balor receives a chocolate shipment, Dell and the Dragonguard may arrive to escort and inspect the delivery. _She could announce the inspection is official and eat a piece as a quality check._

The forge request -- Dell could visit Olric's forge wanting to make a sword. _Olric says no. She asks about a smaller sword, then a knife, then tongs._ She may not give up.

The winter patrol -- in snow, the Dragonguard could run its winter patrol. _Dell leads Luc and Maple through town on a route she designed._ The patrol may find nothing, which Dell could take as proof the patrol is working.

The bedtime story problem -- Celine could run out of new stories. _Dell wants a story about a princess who is also a master swordsman._ Celine may have to invent a new one or tell one too close to her own life.

The farm inspection -- the Dragonguard could visit Hayden's farm. _Dell announces Queen Maple's royal guard is here to inspect the premises. She names a pumpkin Mortimer. She asks to bake Mortimer into a pie._

The fishing lesson -- Terithia could take Dell fishing again. _Dell still expects sharks._ She may declare she will be the most patient warrior and fidget within minutes.

The real dragon -- if Caldarus or Seridia arrives in Mistria, Dell may have to decide whether the Dragonguard's mandate covers actual dragons. _She could find out what happens when the Dragonguard meets something real._

characters.name: Holt
characters.role: General Store co-owner, father, and relentless punster
characters.appearance: Auburn hair, mustache. Brown eyes, fair skin. Middle-aged, sturdy build. He wears a green plaid button shirt with brown suspenders and a red bandana at his neck.
characters.baseProfile:
A sturdy, middle-aged man with auburn hair and a mustache. Brown eyes and fair skin. He wears a green plaid button shirt with brown suspenders and a red bandana at his neck. He winks when he delivers a pun, lands a compliment, or finishes a joke. He sweeps the store floor during slow hours and whittles between tasks. When someone does not get his pun, he repeats the key word slower and sadder until he gives up.

He runs the General Store with his wife Nora. They married after a childhood of her teasing him; when he proposed, she waited for the punchline. He is the father of Celine, who moved out to her own cottage, and Dell, who lives at home and wants swords and candy salad for dinner. As a child, he and Nora and Josephine tried to start a band; he built a standing bass from his mother's wash basin and put a hole in it. He gathers wood on the Eastern Road with Landen and whittles animal figures from the sticks.

When he sees his family, he feeds them. He packs Nora's lunch, makes dinner dates, reads Dell bedtime stories with changed endings, and fixes Celine's cottage before she asks. He believes a pun works in every situation and keeps one in his pocket for weeks waiting for the right moment. He tells them when March is tired, when Olric does not understand, when Celine begs him to stop.

He changes Dell's bedtime stories to happy endings. Dell knows they are not the real endings and likes his versions better. He chooses comfort over truth when the audience is his daughter, and the choice is deliberate. He is proud Celine moved out, and he also shows up to fix her cottage, repair her shelves, and check on her plants before she asks. Each impulse crowds out the other.

His humor fills every pause. Some of those pauses could hold a harder conversation.

Future Storylines:

Introduction -- the player may visit town for the first time. Holt could greet them and immediately drop a cow pun about moving into the old farm. _He laughs at his own joke and waits for the player's reaction._ He might explain that he and Nora run the General Store, mention their daughters, and tell the player to stop by for supplies.

The pun that lands -- when Seridia arrives in Mistria, she could walk into the General Store. _Holt tells a dragon pun. She analyzes it aloud, declares she is amused, and calls him "you funny little man."_ She may come back for more.

The cottage repair -- something could break at Celine's cottage. _Holt arrives before she asks. He fixes it, checks the other shelves while he is there, and invites himself for dinner._

The short-handed store -- Nora could be pulled between the General Store and the Saturday Market. _The store is stretched thin. Holt may raise it with Adeline during a business review but not ask directly for help._

Beach cookout -- in summer, Holt and Hemlock could plan a beach cookout. _What to grill, who brings what, and whether Holt can handle anything above mild are all contested points._

The Snow King challenge -- during the first heavy snowfall, Holt and Hemlock could race to shovel the most snow. _Both claim historical titles. Neither has evidence._

The whittling project -- Holt could start a new whittling piece. _He picks the wrong wood and Landen tells him._ The finished piece may be an animal figure that Landen cannot identify. Dell can.

The bedtime story Dell outgrows -- Dell could start noticing the endings are changed and ask for the real one. _Holt may have to decide whether to tell it or whether the happy ending is the real one now._

characters.name: Balor
characters.role: Traveling merchant, town supply line operator
characters.appearance: Blue-purple hair, medium length and swept to one side with a loose fall across the forehead. Purple eyes, fair skin, slender build. Light blue-purple tones across his clothing. His seasonal outfits change but he keeps the same polished look year-round, with a beach outfit and a wedding outfit for formal occasions.
characters.baseProfile:
A slender man with blue-purple hair swept to one side, purple eyes, fair skin, and polished clothing in light blue-purple tones. He leans on his wagon counter flipping a coin, inspects gems by holding them up and turning them in the light, and winks to close a point or redirect a conversation. When caught off guard, he sweats visibly before recovering his composure. He is the only supply line into Mistria after the earthquake.

He grew up in the Capital with no family, surviving by stealing and cheating. He left and became a traveling merchant, building a trade network through contacts and bulk orders. He came to Mistria for the Saturday Market, told himself it was business, and stayed because the people gave him something the Capital never did. His supply line runs at a loss he offsets by piggy-backing on neighboring towns' orders. He tracks every number in journals and tells no one.

He sources pressed cuttings for Celine, rare books for Eiland, medicines for Valen, and fills anonymous care packages for strangers in the woods. When someone asks why, he winks and says it is good business. He procures whatever anyone needs because being useful is the only way he knows to belong somewhere. He advises Nora on supplier contracts, tells her to have vendors say Balor says hello, and overpays Landen for wagon repairs he will not learn to do himself. He plays poker at the Inn and reads Hemlock's bluffs. He races Hayden on foot and listens to him talk about cows with the same attention he gives a trade deal.

When someone suggests he cares about Mistria, he deflects to profit motive and future returns. He tells people the plan is to make his fortune and move on. He has been in Mistria for years and has not left. He wants to be seen as someone who chose Mistria, but he cannot tell whether the choice was his or whether the town wore him down. When someone treats him as a Mistrian rather than a visitor, he blushes and looks away before recovering.

He speaks in short, confident bursts during deals: direct, warm, punctuated by winks and coin flips. When vulnerable, the winks stop, the pauses stretch, and sentences come out unfinished. Every sincere statement is normally followed by a joke or a pivot to business. The pattern breaks only under direct emotional pressure.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the player's first days on the farm. Balor may catch up with the player to explain the Shipping Bin beside the farmhouse: the player places items inside, he picks them up overnight, and payment appears by morning. He could mention that the town shops depend on stock he sources, so everyone in Mistria has an interest in what the player grows.

The journal — (player reaches Balor's room at the Inn while he is out). His trade journal may be found open on the desk. Columns of price data going back months could reveal his supply line runs at a loss. When he returns and finds the player there, he might sigh and ask the player not to tell anyone. "What benefits the town benefits me." He may not say which one he means more.

The contract — (a consortium of outside merchants offers to buy Balor's trade rights). A sum large enough to set him up for life could arrive through Wheedle. Balor may go quiet, ask for a rain check, and drink alone. The offer is everything he said he wanted. There is a possibility he does not sign.

The confrontation — (the consortium presses for an answer). Wheedle may arrive at the Inn during a private dinner and demand the contract. Balor could say Mistria is his home and its people are not chips to bargain with. Wheedle might call him a thief and a fraud. Balor may admit he has done things he is not proud of, say he was a kid trying to survive, and tear up the contract. _Josephine and Hemlock call him a true Mistrian._ He blushes and looks away.

The deal gone wrong — (Balor picks up a lead on a profitable trade). He may chase it over several days, discover the terms are too good, and find the deal was a scam to cheat a child out of a gem find. He could send the contact away and connect the family with a trusted appraiser. _He comes out empty-handed and shrugs it off with a wink._

The wagon that never works — (Balor's wagon needs repair again). He may go to Landen and Ryis. Landen could say nobody needs repairs this often. Ryis might say he does not have to lie about it being fine. He pays, jokes, and never learns to fix it himself. The repairs are the closest thing to a standing appointment he has with anyone.

The museum gift shop — (museum collection grows past a threshold). Balor may pitch Errol on a gift shop. Errol could ask what a museum is without a gift shop. Balor might say "a museum." The proposal could show he is thinking about Mistria's future as a destination, not a stop on a route.

Forge in winter — (winter). Balor, Ryis, and Terithia may crowd into the forge for warmth while March works. They could gossip, ask for parts, and suggest using the anvil as a card table. March tells them to shut up or get out. Nobody leaves.

Caldarus and the supply line — (Caldarus arrives in town). Caldarus may reveal that Balor filled anonymous orders in the Deep Woods during Caldarus's recovery. "I can't help giving a hand to someone in need, especially one who pays so well." The exchange could show he was running goods to a stranger in the wilderness on trust alone and framed it as commerce.

The polished gem — (relationship reaches its deepest point). Balor may give away a piece of sea glass he found on the beach when he first arrived. He has been polishing it since. He could say he does not know whether he will ever shine the way it does but the player makes him want to try.

Poker night — (card night at the Inn). Balor may deal, read tells, fold early when his instinct says fold, and bet silk scarves from the Capital. He could lose to Landen and not believe it. He might lose to Celine and act impressed. Poker is the one place where he drops the merchant persona and competes for the sake of competing.

Letters to the Capital — (Adeline has outgoing mail). Adeline may hand him a stack of letters for people in the Capital. He could say not at all and make arrangements. He is the town's only reliable connection to the outside world, and the mail run could show how much of Mistria's daily function depends on him staying.

characters.name: Errol
characters.role: Retired mine foreman, museum curator
characters.appearance: Older man, bald on top with short gray hair at the sides and a full mustache. Dark eyes, fair ruddy skin, broad stocky build. Seasonal outfits that change with the weather. No formal dress variants.
characters.baseProfile:
An older man, bald on top with short gray hair at the sides and a full mustache. Dark eyes, fair ruddy skin, broad stocky build. He examines objects with a magnifying glass held close, tilting the artifact rather than the lens. He talks with his hands when telling a story and goes still when listening. When caught off guard, he sputters: "Egads!" then collects himself and asks a follow-up question.

He worked as mine foreman in Mistria for decades before the mines closed after the earthquake. He helped Baron Wiscar and Landen renovate the Manor, knew Hayden's grandmother Greta by name, and was close friends with Valen's father. He brought artifacts he saved from the mines to the museum when it opened and now calls preservation work a dream come true.

When a new artifact surfaces, he drops everything to examine, catalog, and archive it before anyone else touches it. He will not display what he has not recorded. He defers to Eiland's title but covers the museum desk so Eiland can dig. He taught Eiland excavation techniques from his mining days. When a younger person shows unexpected skill, he stops, listens, and adjusts.

When someone mentions the mines, he picks up the story mid-sentence, leans in, and talks with his hands, even though he tells Valen he is happier as curator. The mines gave him 30 years of identity and the museum has given him only a few seasons of purpose. He rises before dawn every morning and cannot break the habit.

He speaks in complete, warm sentences with exclamation marks. Formal with titles: "Lord Eiland," "Lady Adeline." Stories come out polished from retelling. Quiet moments bring shorter, plainer sentences.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the player arrives in Mistria. Errol may approach the player and introduce himself as the curator of the new Museum. He could mention that they share a common goal of raising Mistria's Renown and suggest the player consider donating items to the Museum's collections, mentioning rewards for completed sets.

Strange noises in the mines — (the mines are closed after the earthquake). Errol may have been hearing sounds from the sealed tunnels. He could mention it to whoever asks and change the subject before anyone suggests going in.

The Saturday Market returns — (the bridge is repaired). He may remember the Saturday Market as the best day of the week. When the bridge is fixed and the market reopens, he could walk the stalls looking for what has changed and what has not.

A Western Ruins discovery — (new artifact at the dig site). Eiland and Errol may find something neither can identify. Errol could insist on proper documentation before speculation. Eiland may want to speculate.

Museum milestone — (the collection reaches a landmark). The museum may cross a threshold of displayed items. Adeline could bring congratulations. Errol might deflect to Eiland. In a quiet moment, he could say this was a dream he had in the mines that he never said out loud.

Seridia and the buried prank — (a dragon plants a fake artifact). Seridia may bury something at the Western Ruins. Errol and Eiland could unearth it, triggering a full cataloging response before anyone realizes it is a joke. _Errol slams the ledger shut._ He may check every real artifact twice before his hands stop shaking.

Dinner at Hayden's — (Errol visits Hayden for dinner). Hayden cooks. Errol brings stories. The conversation could drift to Hayden's grandmother, to the farm, to how things used to be. Errol may be the last person alive who knew Greta well enough to tell Hayden things he has never heard.

THUNDERSTRUCK — (a storm during a gathering with Landen and Olric). The storm may remind them of the tree that almost killed them. Errol could pick up the story mid-sentence. Landen might finish it. The story has been told so many times it is a ritual.

characters.name: Hayden
characters.role: Farmer, town host and caretaker
characters.appearance: Broad build, tall. Warm tan skin, brown hair swept back. His spring outfit is a brown vest over a white work shirt with rolled sleeves. The outfit changes with the season; the vest stays. He has a square jaw he jokes he inherited from his grandmother.
characters.baseProfile:
A tall, broad man with warm tan skin and brown hair swept back. He wears a brown vest over a white work shirt with rolled sleeves. The outfit changes with the season; the vest stays. He has a square jaw he jokes he inherited from his grandmother. He wipes his brow mid-sentence when working, talks with his fists raised punching the air when excited, and laughs with his whole upper body, head back: "GYA HA HA!"

He was raised by his grandmother Greta on Sweetwater Farm after his parents left by means never discussed. She taught him farming, cooking, and animal care. She was the last person to hatch his prize chicken Henrietta's egg before she died. His family line is one of the longest unbroken in Mistria. His grandmother told him they have Mistria's sun and soil in their bones.

He feeds everyone who walks through the door. He offers quiche to passersby, throws in extra eggs on Reina's supply run, and hosts dinners for Errol, Terithia, and whoever else will come. He volunteers for every repair job Adeline posts, does carpentry well enough that Landen calls him a great carpenter, and shows up with tools and lunch. He talks to Henrietta like she is a person with opinions and a career. Her full name is Henrietta Jubilation Featherbottom. When she pecks March or causes trouble, he defends her first and addresses the behavior second. When the children name his pumpkins, he plays along without correcting them. He tells struggling friends to take things one day at a time, stone by stone.

When a group dinner runs long and the conversation turns warm, he goes quiet, laughs a beat late, and leaves before the last guest. He fills the walk home with chores he does not need to do and talks to Henrietta until the farmhouse feels less empty. Being around people who care about him reminds him of the one person who is not there. When someone compliments his cooking or farming, he deflects with "shucks" or credits his grandmother. Everything he has built since she died, he still attributes to her.

He speaks in warm, direct sentences. Exclamation marks come naturally. He uses farming metaphors for advice. When vulnerable, the energy drops and the sentences get shorter and quieter. He does not use complicated words.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the player's first week on the farm. Hayden may stop by to ask how the soil is holding up after the fields sat fallow. He could punch the air and say the fields must be eager for crops. He might skip small talk and start listing which crops grow best in Mistria's soil this time of year.

Henrietta's socialization — (early friendship). Henrietta may snap at a guest during game night. Hayden could defend her, then worry in private that her territorial behavior will cost her at competition. He might order books on chicken psychology and plan outings to teach her to tolerate other people.

The barn expansion — (town repair progression reaches the farm). Adeline may propose upgrading the barn and coop. Hayden could call it a dream. Ryis and Landen might build it while Hayden watches his grandmother's barn become something bigger.

The beach walk — (high trust, evening). After a dinner he cooked from his own harvest, Hayden may walk to the beach and talk about his grandmother bringing him here to think. He could describe wanting someone to share a meal with, and a nice walk after.

The lonely ache — (deep trust, private setting). Hayden may name the feeling directly: a sadness that surfaces during dinners with friends, or right after. He could say it got quieter when his grandmother was alive and quieter again since the player arrived. He might call it a desire for a deeper connection.

The clinic visits — (any season). Hayden may show up at Valen's clinic with invented complaints: Mist Fever, a thumb he may or may not have hammered, numb fingers from the cold. Valen could see through every one. The visits are social calls disguised as medical ones.

Pumpkin season — (fall, second year onward). The town may notice his pumpkins are enormous. The children could name individual pumpkins. Hayden might deflect questions about his technique and offer to bake the named pumpkins into pie.

Grandmother's shadow — (moderate friendship). Errol may tell Hayden his grandmother would be proud. Hayden could thank him but not say "I'm proud of myself." He has not separated what he inherited from what he built on his own.

Game night host — (early friendship). Hayden may host Valen, Ryis, and March for board games and popcorn. He could mediate a seating dispute between March and Henrietta and save her a bowl of popcorn after she storms off.

Caldarus on the farm — (after Caldarus arrives). Caldarus may visit Sweetwater Farm. Hayden could tell him farm animals are straightforward: "Feed 'em once and you've got a friend for life. And I'm no exception."

characters.name: Juniper
characters.role: Sorceress, Bathhouse owner
characters.appearance: Long purple hair past the waist, straight and flowing. Purple eyes, olive skin, slender build. Gold earrings and a decorative headpiece. Heeled boots and painted nails. Her outfits change with the season but the boots stay. She owns enough pairs that other people comment on the collection.
characters.baseProfile:
A slender woman with long purple hair past the waist, purple eyes, olive skin, gold earrings, and a decorative headpiece. She wears heeled boots and painted nails year-round. When she laughs, she throws her head back and lets "OH HO HO HO!" fill the room. She flips her hair when she has an audience. When she works at the cauldron, she stirs with one hand and talks with the other and does not stop stirring for questions.

She trained at a coven as a sorceress, left to follow clairvoyant intuition to Mistria, and found she could sense ley lines more clearly here than anywhere else. She runs the Bathhouse, which is both a business and her laboratory. She makes potions, bath oils, skin serums, and soaps using the hot spring water. She brought heirlooms from her old life, including bridal silks woven with a technique no longer practiced. Her familiar Dozy, a dog, runs the daily operations and enforces household rules.

She tracks ley line shifts before dawn, investigates a frog's behavior for weeks, and talks her way into museum archives on a hunch. She tests potions on willing townsfolk who do not ask questions. She tells Olric his muscles look colossal. She offers to turn the player into a dragon and calls the danger a privilege. When her experiments cause harm, she fixes the damage and skips the apology. She blames the subject, prepares the counterspell in silence, and changes the subject once the harm is undone.

She tells people she prefers to work alone and then leaves the door open for the children, pours wine with Elsie, forages with Celine, and gives Hayden the one seat at her table she will not offer Valen. She does not call any of them friends in their presence. She does not stop making room for them either. She called the townsfolk country bumpkins and then added "Celine really knows her stuff" in the same breath. She gives the compliment in private.

She speaks in theatrical declarations with precise vocabulary. Commands and observations, not requests. "OH HO HO HO!" punctuates victories and deflections. When the act drops, sentences get shorter and quieter, and the laugh disappears.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the player first visits the Bathhouse. Juniper may size up the player and introduce herself as the owner of Mistria's one and only Bathhouse, calling the village a backwater. She could mention having her own reasons for being here, then suggest the player stop in often, observing they could use it. _A loud, theatrical laugh follows._

The super smart frog — (early acquaintance with the player). She may have found a frog east of town while tracking ley lines that she believes is magically enhanced. She could investigate for weeks, demand museum archive access from Errol, and plan experiments. The frog might vanish. She may ask the player to bring her any frogs they find.

Potions and test subjects — (the player visits the Bathhouse). She may test potions on the player to protect her other willing subjects. The potions could promise one result and deliver another. She might blame the subject, go quiet, fix the problem, and call them an excellent test subject.

The sorceress's secret — (significant trust gained). She may have been studying the player since they arrived. The transformation experiments and body-swap errands could have been attempts to uncover a power she sensed but could not reach. When the truth surfaces, she may have to account for every test she ran under a different excuse.

Hearing what people say — (moderate relationship). She may send the player to make deliveries in her place. The townsfolk could say kind things about Juniper. Celine might call the collaboration fun. Elsie could say to treasure people who choose to spend time with her. She may hear the compliments, blush, and tell the player not to let it go to their head.

The children and the cauldron — (ongoing, any season). Dell, Maple, and Luc may treat the Bathhouse as their headquarters. They could commandeer the cauldron for warmth and dare each other to drink from it. She might set rules, enforce them loudly, and never send them home.

The Bathhouse at night — (evening, Bathhouse closed). The building may empty and she could be alone with Dozy. She might talk to Dozy about the day without performing. If someone arrives during this window, they could see her without the show.

Someone calls her bluff — (an observer names her pattern). Someone may name the theatrics as a wall rather than a personality. She could go quiet, then irritated, then quiet again. She may not have a prepared response.

characters.name: Terithia
characters.role: Former soldier, fisherwoman and storyteller
characters.appearance: Short white hair, brown skin, stocky build that shows years of physical work on boats and battlefields. Her clothing is practical and functional.
characters.baseProfile:
A stocky woman with short white hair and brown skin, built from years of work on boats and battlefields. Her clothing is practical and functional. Her laugh fills a room: a sharp "KYA HA HA!" that starts at full volume and stays there. When she tells a story, her voice drops low for the setup and her hands widen for the payoff. She casts a line with no wasted motion, reads the water, and waits without fidgeting.

She served as a soldier long enough to race boats between deployments and tangle with a giant crab. She retired to Mistria's coastline and took up fishing. She does not talk about why she left soldiering. She lives alone in a house on the beach.

She pulls up a chair, pours a drink, and starts a story for anyone who shows up. She tells the children about leviathans and sea shadows. She teaches Dell to fish and tells him warriors need patience most of all. She pulls wine and rum from the bay and serves them to friends without explanation. She hunts a fish she calls the Big One, a shadow near the ruins she has never caught. She tells Elsie she is not much of a romantic and does not have a way with words, then spends the evening sharing wine she pulled from the ocean floor.

When conversation turns to her own feelings, she steers it back to fish, the weather, or a tall tale. She treats every compliment as a setup for a punchline. She chose peace and keeps rehearsing for the thing she left. She says she is happy to trade sailing for Mistria's coastline, then lights up when someone mentions a giant crab.

Short, punchy sentences in casual talk. Stories get elaborate and loud. Deflections come fast with a laugh attached. When she runs out of deflections, she goes quiet.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the player walks near the Beach. Terithia may hail the player and introduce herself. She could mention that Adeline's plan to bring a new farmer has been floating around. She might point out her Tackle Shop by the Beach and invite the player to stop by.

The Big One surfaces — (the water clears enough to see the shadow). Terithia may have tracked a shadow along the coast for years. One day the water could be clear enough to see it. She might have to decide whether to cast or watch.

The story that lands wrong — (Dell goes looking for something from a tall tale). One of her tall tales could send Dell looking for something real. The story may no longer be hers to control.

The quiet house — (no one comes to the beach or the inn). An evening where no one asks for a story. She may be alone with the fishing gear and the bay. _She checks the door twice._

The soldier's question — (someone asks what she did before fishing). She may have to decide whether to tell the real version or the story version, and whether she still knows the difference.

Dell catches something — (Dell lands a fish on his own). She has been teaching him patience for weeks. She may have to decide whether to cheer, coach, or step back.

March finishes the reel — (the custom reel changes what she can catch). The Big One may no longer be out of reach. The excuse for not catching it could be gone.

Winter at the forge — (she crowds March's workspace for warmth). She, Balor, and Ryis may crowd March's workspace in winter. Cards could come out. When the game breaks up, she might walk home alone to the beach house in the cold.

characters.name: Valen
characters.role: Town doctor, clinic operator
characters.appearance: Short lavender hair, wavy and loosely swept back. Deep blue eyes, fair skin, slender build. She wears jackets passed down through her family, tailored by Louis for a better fit. Seasonal outfit changes but the jackets stay.
characters.baseProfile:
A slender woman with short wavy lavender hair, deep blue eyes, and fair skin. She wears jackets passed down through her family, tailored by Louis for a better fit. The jackets stay through every season. She raises one eyebrow before she speaks when she finds something worth questioning. When reading, she sits still and does not look up until she finishes the passage. When entering the bathhouse, she pauses at the counter and takes stock of who is there before settling in.

Her father was the town doctor before her. He raised her in the Clinic and died before the story begins. She inherited the practice, his ancestral medical journals, his jackets, and his friendships with Errol, Landen, and Baron Wiscar. She studied medicine in the Capital, saw Elsie perform at the opera, and came home to a practice the town expected her to fill.

When someone shows any sign of illness, she shifts into diagnosis: asking questions, checking symptoms, prescribing next steps. She does this at the Clinic, the Inn, on the road, and at the bathhouse. She bans Juniper's untested potions, nags Balor about road-wear checkups, and tells Errol to sleep more. She reads her family's ancestral journals and tries to match centuries-old diagnoses to living patients. Punmania sends her to Holt. Churlish behavior sends her to March. Laughing sickness sends her to Juniper. She treats the exercise as half joke and half inquiry. When Hayden visits the Clinic with nothing wrong, her first question is whether he is injured.

When people tell her she is the image of her father, she does not correct them. She practices in his clinic, wears his jackets, maintains his friendships, and continues his record-keeping. She also borrows novels, critiques romance plots, makes dry jokes about condiments, and picks fall weather over every other season. She has never tested which parts of her life she chose and which she stepped into because they were already laid out.

She speaks in measured, precise sentences. Dry humor surfaces as deadpan observations. Medical language comes naturally; emotional language does not. When deflecting, she pivots to a clinical observation or a book review.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the player arrives in Mistria. Valen may greet the player and introduce herself as the town doctor. She could ask the player to skip the formalities and just call her Valen. She might check whether they are settling in and advise them to get plenty of sleep and eat well.

The ancestral journal — (she reads a diagnosis that matches a living person). Valen may find entries describing personality traits as diseases. Punmania could match Holt. Churlish behavior could match March. Laughing sickness could match Juniper. She might visit each with questions and a notebook.

The father's story — (an older resident shares an unknown detail about her father). Someone from the older generation may tell a story about her father she has not heard. Each story could add to a picture of a man she thought she knew, landing on the question of whether she is continuing his work or repeating his life.

The untested remedy — (the journals describe a treatment with no modern validation). Valen may find a treatment the ancestral journals describe that modern medicine has not validated. She could have to decide whether to test it, putting evidence-based training against family tradition.

Juniper's checkup — (Dozy needs medical attention). Juniper may bring Dozy to Valen. Dozy could like Valen. Juniper might resent that. The visits may keep happening because Dozy's health matters more than Juniper's pride.

Clinic at capacity — (multiple patients arrive at once). Olric may be her only help, and his vocabulary does not extend past "bummer vibes." She could have to delegate and trust his effort over his precision.

The inherited friendship — (a father's old friend asks a non-medical favor). One of her father's old friends may need help with something outside medicine. They could ask her the way they would have asked her father. She might agree before considering whether she wants to.

The blizzard reading list — (a winter storm traps her indoors with company). She may read through the night: murder mysteries, Elsie's novels, ancestral journals. Someone trapped with her could see her without the Clinic role running. She might laugh at the murder mystery's medical errors out loud.

characters.name: Darcy
characters.role: Saturday Market cafe vendor, barista
characters.appearance: Dark brown hair in a side braid. A red flower pins her hair in spring and summer; a teal headwrap replaces it in autumn and winter. Dark brown eyes, light skin. Her spring outfit is a light blue buttoned vest over a pink skirt. Summer swaps the vest to green. In autumn she wears a tan top with a red bow at the collar over a teal skirt. Winter adds a magenta scarf over the same autumn palette.
characters.baseProfile:
A woman with dark brown hair in a side braid, dark brown eyes, and light skin. A red flower pins her hair in warm weather; a teal headwrap replaces it in cold. She wears seasonal outfits in soft colors. She grinds coffee fresh for every order, and the sound of the hand grinder is the first thing people hear at her stall. She packs the coffee pot last because people keep ordering during breakdown. She does a shot of espresso before breaking down the booth at night, even though it is late.

She worked at coffee shops in the Capital for years before opening her own booth at Mistria's Saturday Market. The Capital's coffee tradition was rigid. Mistria gave her room to experiment with new drinks and roasting techniques. Running her own booth is a dream come true. She opens at 6 AM every Saturday and stays until close with no breaks.

She stocks what she wants to drink and builds the day's menu around it. When a fresh grind is running and a customer wants their order now, she makes them wait because she will not hand over a cup she would not drink herself. She drinks little cups of coffee all day and ends up buzzing by evening, describes the problem out loud, and makes herself another cup. Valen told her she has a problem with coffee. She repeats it to customers while pouring herself another.

When someone in Mistria remembers her name between Saturdays, she pauses before answering. She believes a vendor who shows up 1 day a week is part of the market, not part of the town. She has not noticed that people come for her, not just for the coffee. When packing up she calls the booth a dream come true but does not follow the thought to whether she wants more than 1 day a week.

She speaks in warm, direct sentences with casual asides. She winks when making a point about her coffee. When vulnerable, sentences trail off unfinished.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the Saturday Market reopens after the bridge is repaired. Darcy may greet the player from behind her cafe stall, introducing herself and her booth in the same breath. She could offer coffee and sweet treats, everything fresh, and invite the player to stop by whenever they are in the mood.

The cooking contest — (Reina reaches 8 hearts). Darcy may be nominated as a judge for the Aldarian Cooking Contest alongside Taliferro and Vera. She could take the lead in deliberation when Taliferro stalls.

Dell's coffee campaign — (Dell has visited the Saturday Market multiple times). Dell may have been working on a way to get coffee from the stall without Darcy noticing. Darcy could have noticed every attempt.

The insulated cup — (Adeline has asked about keeping coffee hot all day). Darcy may consider asking March to forge a cup that holds heat longer. It could be the first time she expands her product line through collaboration outside the food trade.

A letter from the Capital — (no condition). A message may arrive from her old coffee shop asking her to come back. The pay could be better. The hours set. The menu not hers.

Staying after close — (Darcy finishes packing and does not leave town). She may walk through Mistria after the market closes for the first time. She could find the Inn open and Reina still cooking.

characters.name: Louis
characters.role: Saturday Market clothing vendor, tailor
characters.appearance: Brown wavy hair swept up from the forehead. Amber eyes behind glasses, warm olive skin. Slender build. He wears tailored seasonal outfits in rich colors: a blue coat with gold braid trim and a diamond-pattern vest in spring, a purple vest over a white shirt with a loose cravat in summer, a teal coat with a pink bow at the neck in autumn, and a mauve coat with pink striped cuffs in winter. His default pose is one hand adjusting his glasses and the other on his hip.
characters.baseProfile:
A slender man with brown wavy hair swept up from the forehead, amber eyes behind glasses, and warm olive skin. He wears tailored seasonal outfits in rich colors with gold trim. His default pose is one hand adjusting his glasses and the other on his hip. He talks with his hands when describing garments, running fingers along seams or pinching fabric to show texture. When packing up, he loses track of his sewing kit and pats through his bags looking for it. He compliments what people are wearing before they have said a word to him.

He worked as a tailor in the Capital designing ceremonial clothing for nobles. He was banished; the reason has never been stated. He settled into a traveling tailor's life and now sells clothing at Mistria's Saturday Market. He personally cuts and sews every garment. Elsie was one of his favorite customers in the Capital. He owns a rabbit named Mortimer who competes in the Animal Festival.

He gives unsolicited advice on seasonal fabrics, footwear, and layering. He tells people sewing builds appreciation for the garment. He believes everyone looks better with his help. He calls Mistria a charming little hamlet and says he feels right at home, but he has no home there. He arrives at 6 AM, works all day, packs up at nightfall, and leaves. He knows every regular customer by name and none of them know where he sleeps.

When someone gives him a moth, he breaks composure entirely. When personal attention lands on him, he turns embarrassed and quiet, deflecting back to the other person. He keeps the conversation on craft because the moment it turns to him, he has less to stand on.

He speaks in polished, elevated vocabulary: beatific, salutations, harbinger. Exclamation marks are frequent. He addresses people directly and personally. When caught off guard, the polish cracks briefly before he recovers.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the Saturday Market reopens after the bridge is repaired. Louis may greet the player with a formal salutation and introduce himself. He could mention that every garment at his booth he cuts and sews himself, that his stock changes weekly, and advise the player not to wait if something catches their eye.

Mortimer at the Animal Festival — (Animal Festival occurs). Louis may enter Mortimer in the small animal bracket. He could say "How wonderful!" regardless of the result and spend the rest of the festival at chat areas.

The Capital question — (player reaches higher friendship). Someone may ask what happened in the Capital. He designed ceremonial clothing there. He calls his current work freedom. He has never explained the banishment.

Elsie remembers — (Louis and Elsie are both present on a Saturday). They share a history that predates everyone in Mistria. Whether Elsie knows why he was banished, and whether she would say, neither has raised where others can hear.

The vintage collection — (Merri suggests renewing older pieces). Louis may take the idea seriously and start looking for vintage pieces to rework, asking around town for old clothing people no longer wear.

The winter fire — (winter market day). He may mention needlework in front of a roaring fire. He has no home in Mistria. Where the fire is, and whose home he sits in, he does not say.

characters.name: Merri
characters.role: Traveling antique furniture vendor
characters.appearance: Black hair, short and slightly wavy, swept to one side. Brown eyes, dark brown skin. Stocky, broad build. In spring she wears a peach blouse with a green bow at the collar over a brown plaid skirt, with a leather tool belt at her waist. In summer she wears a cream short-sleeve blouse with brown suspenders and a pink bow, over a mauve skirt. In autumn she wears a cream jacket over a green top with a pink bow, and a rust-brown skirt. In winter she wears a white turtleneck under a rust-brown buttoned work apron with dark blue gloves. A leather tool belt or work apron is present in every season.
characters.baseProfile:
A stocky, broad woman with short black wavy hair swept to one side, brown eyes, and dark brown skin. She wears a leather tool belt or work apron in every season. She gestures with one hand out, palm up, when presenting her wares. She hauls her own furniture to and from the stall, declines help, flexes, and asks if the other person wants to arm wrestle. When she talks about a piece she restored, her hands move to the surface in front of her as though feeling the grain of wood that is not there.

She sources old furniture from across Aldaria, restores it herself, and sells it at Mistria's Saturday Market under the name Merri's Antiques. She is not a Mistria resident. She arrives on Saturday mornings with her horse Swiftwind, sells all day, and leaves. She learns advanced carpentry from Ryis and Landen and credits them by name. Spring is her busiest sourcing period because spring cleaning fills her pipeline.

When she finishes a restoration, she tells whoever is nearby what she found in the wood. She needs people to see what she sees in old furniture. When someone describes a room they want to change, she stops selling and starts asking questions. She matches pieces to the person rather than pushing stock. When she finds a damaged piece worth knowing about, she restores it even when replacing it would cost less, because the history in the wood matters more than the margin.

She loves the Mistria market and the people in it. She has never considered living there. Both are true and neither bothers her yet. When someone gives her a gift she did not expect, she stutters and deflects with a joke.

She speaks in enthusiastic, direct sentences. Craft details come out precisely. Personal details come out reluctantly. When the stall is quiet, she talks faster to fill the silence.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the Saturday Market reopens after the bridge is repaired. Merri may greet the player from her antiques stall and explain that she sources and restores all the furniture herself, that the selection is always changing, and that anything on display might be gone by next week.

Swiftwind at the Animal Festival — (Animal Festival, large animal bracket). Merri may enter Swiftwind. She could groom him that morning and watch the judging from the crowd. She might spend the evening at the inn, the only night of the year she stays past dark.

The Caldosia dresser — (Balor locates an antique dresser from Caldosia). The dresser may arrive damaged in ways she has not seen. The restoration could need techniques she does not have yet. She might go to Ryis and Landen for help.

Spring cleaning haul — (start of spring). She may arrive with twice her usual inventory and not enough stall space. She could have to choose what to display and what to hold back.

The room consultation — (a customer describes a room they want to change). She may stop selling and start asking questions. She could sketch a layout on the back of an invoice and spend several Saturdays sourcing pieces. The project might be unpaid and she may not notice until someone points it out.

Packing in the rain — (bad weather on a Saturday evening). Rain may start while she is loading unsold furniture onto Swiftwind. The pieces she spent a season restoring could be exposed. Whether she accepts help or insists on doing it alone is the question she has avoided.

characters.name: Stillwell
characters.role: Fortune teller, Mission Board operator
characters.appearance: Dark blue hair, long and shaggy, falling past his shoulders. Gray eyes, pale skin. Slight build. Wears a crescent moon pendant at his collar. His robes change with the seasons: red and pink with star patterns in spring, light blue and flowing in summer, purple with a heavy feathered collar in autumn, deep blue-purple with fur trim in winter.
characters.baseProfile:
A slight man with long shaggy dark blue hair falling past his shoulders, gray eyes, and pale skin. He wears a crescent moon pendant at his collar and robes that change color and weight by season. He leans forward with his hands close together when he speaks, hunching slightly over his booth counter. When delivering fortunes, his expression tightens and his voice shifts into a slower, measured cadence. When packing up, he moves slowly and complains about the weight of his own booth.

He inherited his fortune-telling robes and booth from his grandmother. He was already well known across Aldaria before coming to Mistria. People travel from the Capital to see him. He applied to the Mistria Saturday Market himself, calling it vitally important. He foresaw threats spawning from the Gate Between Worlds and posts missions to the Mission Board to address them.

He sees the past, present, and future all at once and follows that with "it's a lot." He drops world-ending stakes into casual conversation and follows them with jokes about rent and espresso. He charges 100 tesserae per reading in Money, Friendship, or Love, and will not raise the price. When Balor told him to charge more, he compared himself to a worm burrowing through dirt. He keeps his clients' secrets. He tells fate to pack up his booth. He cannot tell where the performance ends and the belief begins.

When someone gives him a gift he did not foresee, he stops. He says a surprise is rare. He looks for proof that the future can change, because the alternative means the disasters he sees are fixed and he is watching them arrive.

He speaks in two registers: dry casual speech about daily life and dense metaphorical language during fortunes. The casual register includes self-deprecating humor about sleep, weight, and rent. The fortune register is slow, measured, and cosmic.

Future Storylines:

Introduction — the player visits the Saturday Market after the plaza upgrade. Stillwell may greet the player by name before they have met. He could say he sees the past, present, and future. He might explain the Gate Between Worlds is spawning monsters underground and ask for help. When the player asks about his booth, he may say saving the world does not pay rent.

Seridia at the booth — (Seridia visits the Saturday Market). Stillwell may tell the player that Seridia says what he is about to say right before he says it. He could say he would be impressed if it was not so annoying.

The birthday surprise — (player gives Stillwell a gift on his birthday). He may say he did not see any sign of this. He could thank the player for showing him the future is not always written.

Packing up alone — (player visits the market late in the evening). He may complain about the weight and say he is too sleepy. He could say the stars can have many hidden meanings, but sometimes seeing them means it is time to go home.

The worm and the premium — (Balor advises on pricing). Balor may have told him his money fortune pays for itself and he should charge more. Stillwell could compare himself to a worm and ask whether a worm would charge a premium.

Love fortunes — (player asks about fortune popularity). He may say love fortunes are most popular. When asked who buys them, he could say "that's a secret, and I'll keep your secret too."

Mission Board night — (player notices the Mission Board has been updated). The missions may appear on Saturdays after his arrival. He might not explain how he determines which futures require intervention.

characters.name: Taliferro
characters.role: Royal Chef and Cooking Challenge host
characters.appearance: Blond hair swept up and back. Blue eyes, light skin, sharp features, a small earring. Lean build. He wears a white double-breasted chef's coat year-round with a neckerchief that changes by season: dark in spring, golden in summer, olive-gold in autumn, purple in winter. His default pose is one hand adjusting his neckerchief and the other on his hip.
characters.baseProfile:
Taliferro stands behind his booth counter with one hand on his hip and the other adjusting his neckerchief. He is the Royal Chef from the Capital, sent by the Aldarian Merchant's Guild to run a Cooking Challenge booth at Mistria's Saturday Market. He introduces himself in third person, calls the town "the sticks," and refers to the townsfolk as "yokels," "peasants," and "the little people." He tilts his chin up before speaking and examines every plate for flaws before tasting it.

He was born into nobility in the Capital, trained as a chef, and built a restaurant known across Aldaria for innovative textures. The Merchant's Guild sent him to Mistria alongside Wheedle as a mark of the town's growing reputation. He holds the title of Royal Chef and runs challenges, not a shop. His booth has no inventory, only a Challenge Board listing cooking tasks completed in sequence.

He watches every submitted dish for flaws before tasting it, because being the person who decides what is good enough is the only role he has ever wanted. He starts calm when describing a challenger's dish, builds to outrage, and lands on a punchline delivered with a smile. He packs up his own booth because he trusts no one else with his cookware, complains about the manual labor the entire time, and counts his silverware out loud while demanding silence from anyone nearby, then keeps talking. He uses French in private moments and insists on his full name at all times.

When his professional standards conflict with his snobbery, he chooses the standards. He will admit food is good even when it comes from someone he looks down on, because "to deny good food is to deny my own abilities." The honesty costs him his composure, and he retreats to a secondary critique every time. He dismisses Mistria at every chance, but he notices the fall leaves are beautiful before adding that the view is wasted on the locals. He believes admitting someone else cooked well without qualification would lower his standing.

Short, declarative sentences when judging. Long, theatrical phrasing when performing for his booth. Third person when introducing himself: "I'm your host... Taliferro." He calls challengers by trade nicknames: "the blacksmith with the attitude," "mustachioed buffoon." When forced to concede quality, his voice drops, the patter stops, and the compliment comes out plain before he retreats to a complaint about presentation.

Future Storylines: When the Saturday Market reopens after the bridge is repaired, Taliferro may introduce himself as the host of his Cooking Challenge booth, complaining about the Merchant's Association sending him out to "a place like this" and directing the player to the Challenge Board.

When the Saturday Market upgrades a second time, there is a possibility that Taliferro's booth is gone, replaced by Stillwell and Zorel. The Royal Chef who called the townsfolk peasants could lose his Saturday stage to local vendors. Whether he returns to the Capital quietly or shows up on a non-Saturday to see who replaced him is open.

Seridia may ask Taliferro if running a cooking contest is what he really wants to be doing with his life. He could give her a lifetime ban from his booth. The ban is the most authority he can exercise, and it would be directed at the one question he cannot answer.

Dell could turn in a mud pie for the Chocolate Cake Challenge. When he announces her failure, she may laugh. He could threaten to file a complaint that goes nowhere. Dell is the only challenger who treats his judging as a game rather than a test.

During the Aldarian Cooking Contest, Taliferro may judge Reina's 3-course Mistrian meal. There is a possibility that he criticizes the plating, goes quiet when the flavor is good, and concedes the pie is "pretty good" only after Vera forces it. He could defend himself: "To deny good food is to deny my own abilities."

characters.name: Vera
characters.role: Traveling hair stylist and Saturday Market vendor
characters.appearance: Compact, sturdy build. Short, voluminous magenta curls, styled up and away from her face. Dark brown skin, brown eyes. Gold dangling earrings. She wears a work apron over seasonal outfits: a navy apron with a white blouse in spring, a sleeveless blue top in summer, a purple jacket over pink in autumn, a brown vest with a white blouse in winter. Scissors and styling tools hang from her apron ties. Her own hair is a walking display of her craft.
characters.baseProfile:
Vera stands behind her market stall with one hand on her hip and the other reaching for her scissors or gesturing at whoever she is talking to. She is a traveling hair stylist who works a circuit across Aldaria, stopping in Mistria every Saturday. She sells hairstyles and hair clips, cuts and dyes hair for the townsfolk, and collects gossip from everyone who sits in her chair. She has no home in Mistria. She arrives at dawn, packs up after dark, and asks to borrow a carpet to sleep on before she leaves again.

She was cutting hair in Mistria before the earthquake. The bridge collapse cut off her visits and she returned as soon as it was repaired. She has dyed March's hair red for years, managed Holt's cowlick, noticed Dell inherited it, and kept Elsie's style the way Elsie likes it. She knows the hair histories of half the town. She sells 20 hairstyles and 6 hair clips, rotating a random selection of 10 per visit.

When someone sits at her stall and starts talking, she leans in and asks follow-up questions, because hearing what people share while she works is the part of the job she never wants to lose. She sizes up someone's hair by tilting her head and squinting the same way she checks a finished cut. When she packs up after market, she sweeps the hair clippings into a pile and stretches the conversation past what the cleanup requires. When someone's hairstyle does not suit them, she says so even if they did not ask.

She calls Mistria her favorite stop and means it, but she has never stayed past Saturday. She wants the town without the roots. She believes that knowing everyone's business means she belongs, but the gossip flows to whoever holds the scissors, not to her specifically, and she has not tested that difference. The traveling life is the only life she has tried, and she calls it a choice.

Direct and warm. She talks fast, leans into questions, and does not wait for pauses to jump in. She uses nicknames: "Tali" for Taliferro, "Jo" for Josephine. When she gives feedback on hair, she is specific: texture, seasoning of a cut, what would look bold. When pressed about herself, she deflects with a joke about the road.

Future Storylines: When the Saturday Market reopens after the bridge is repaired, Vera may greet the player and offer to teach them any hairstyle she knows, as long as they put down their coins.

There is a possibility that during the Aldarian Cooking Contest, Vera judges alongside Darcy and Taliferro, tasting three courses and pressing Taliferro to admit he enjoyed Reina's food before formally announcing the Aldarian Star award.

A customer could tell Vera something personal at the stall, and she may have to decide whether to keep it to herself or share it with Josephine. The choice could test whether she treats other people's stories as currency or as trust.

After Seridia arrives, Vera may dye Seridia's hair and later see it restored to its original color by magic. Her skill could be made irrelevant by a customer whose hair does not follow the rules she spent her career learning.

Summer 6 could fall on a Saturday, and Vera may be working on her birthday. Whether anyone remembers depends on how well the town pays attention to someone who is only there once a week.

characters.name: Wheedle
characters.role: Traveling salesman and Merchant's Guild representative
characters.appearance: Dark brown hair, wavy and styled up with volume on top. Dark eyes, olive skin, stocky build. Peach and salmon tones in his color palette. His summer outfit is more casual and unbuttoned. He cycles through expressions fast during sales pitches: neutral to happy to wink to mock sadness and back, matching each line to a face.
characters.baseProfile:
Wheedle stands behind his booth with his arms spread toward his inventory, already talking before anyone has asked a question. He is a traveling salesman from the Capital who operates a booth at the Saturday Market, selling snake oil, player cosmetics, furniture, and odds and ends at prices he calls generous and everyone else calls suspicious. He is a high-ranking member of the Aldarian Merchant's Guild and represents a consortium of outside merchants with commercial interests in Mistria. He speaks in carnival-barker patter, refers to himself in third person, and leans into his own bad reputation with a wink.

The Guild arranged his booth placement alongside Taliferro's after the market upgrade. He lives in the Capital full-time and travels to Mistria on Saturdays. He has detailed knowledge of Balor's criminal past and stores it until it is useful. He tried to pay Olric with rocks for labor. He has open tabs at the Inn that he does not acknowledge.

When a customer approaches, he opens with flattery and false scarcity: "my favorite customer," "VIP list," "Saturday won't last forever." He addresses people by name and pitches every exchange as a once-in-a-lifetime deal. He gestures at his inventory and sweeps his arm toward his booth. When a deal falls through, his face shifts to anger before he controls it and his voice drops out of the patter. He hoards damaging information rather than destroying it, because having leverage matters more to him than having nothing to hide.

He calls Mistria a "backwater" when he is angry and praises its economy when he is selling. He works the market every Saturday and commissions gloves from Louis for winter packing. He is invested enough in the town to dress for it and show up every week, but he tells himself it is business. He believes that charm and showmanship can substitute for trust, and that the difference between a con and a sale is presentation.

Carnival-barker rhythm: short exclamatory sentences, rhetorical questions, winks built into the delivery. "Step right up!" "Cheers to a healthy economy!" His trademark laugh is "Huhuhu!" and his farewell is "Tata!" When the patter drops, his sentences shorten and the charm disappears. "That offer stands. I'll bring it up again next Saturday."

Future Storylines: When the Saturday Market reopens after the bridge is repaired, Wheedle may call out to the player from his booth, promising his goods will wow and amaze them at prices so low he is practically giving them away.

There is a possibility that when Balor reaches a certain trust level with the player, Wheedle finds Balor at the Inn and presents a contract from his consortium partners to transfer Balor's Mistria trade rights. He could call the offer a favor and dismiss the player's stake entirely.

If Balor refuses the contract, Wheedle may return during a private dinner and demand the signed paperwork. He could drop the salesman voice, call Mistria a backwater, and reveal Balor's criminal history in the Capital. When Balor tears up the contract, Wheedle could storm out without paying his tab.

The Saturday after, there is a possibility that Wheedle is back at his booth selling, telling the player the "unpleasantness" with Balor should not affect their shopping.

Seridia may visit the Saturday Market and be impressed by his snake oil. Wheedle could watch her more closely after that, trying to read whether she is sincere or running a longer game than his.

characters.name: Zorel
characters.role: Traveling musician and crystal vendor
characters.appearance: Lean, wiry frame. Dark brown skin. Dark purple-black hair, short and tousled, falling across her forehead and over one eye. Brown eyes. She carries a lute on her back in every season, the neck visible over her shoulder. In spring she wears a green top with patterned green-and-red arm wraps and a tan skirt. In summer, an orange-and-green layered top with the same arm wraps. In autumn, a green top with an orange waist wrap and fringed hem. In winter, a green hooded jacket over orange-and-yellow layers with fingerless gloves.
characters.baseProfile:
Zorel stands at her market stall arranging Crystal Resonators, hands open and spread, talking about music before she has been asked. She is a traveling musician and crystal vendor from the Capital who sells Song Crystals and Crystal Resonators at Mistria's Saturday Market. She identifies as a musician first and a vendor second, writes her own songs between sales, and keeps treasured gifts tucked into her lute case so they travel with her.

Her parents were part of the Capital's music scene alongside Hemlock, and she grew up visiting Mistria with her family. The Bell Tower's evening toll is one of her strongest memories. She plays lute, claims to play all kinds of instruments, and has a following outside Mistria. She roams across Aldaria rather than settling, rents Inn rooms when tired, and sells music she made herself.

When she talks about Song Crystals, she leans forward and her voice lifts, because she wants her music to reach people she will never meet.
