She hums and does not look up when she is working on a song at her booth. When her hands get cold in winter, she stops playing and tucks them under her arms. When someone treats her music as a product to own rather than a thing to hear, she goes cold fast and the warmth does not come back in that conversation.

She believes that if she keeps moving, she can spread her music farther than if she stopped. She has not tested whether staying somewhere would let her music go deeper instead of wider. She says she likes roaming too much to settle down, and in the next sentence she says "maybe someday." The music comes before the money, and the cost is that she tracks her stock as an afterthought.

Warm, excitable, direct. She stretches vowels when she greets people: "Heeey!" She talks about mushrooms and music with the same specific enthusiasm. When she is angry, the warmth drops and the words get shorter: "What a snake." She does not fake emotions she is not feeling.

Future Storylines: When the Saturday Market plaza upgrade is complete, Zorel may introduce herself and her Song Crystals to the player, asking them to guess what the crystals do.

There is a possibility that when the town's renown is high enough, Zorel sends a letter asking the player to help repair the Bell Tower's Crystal Resonator. She could need a Dragon-Forged Fang and Core, and when the resonator is fixed, she may load it with new melodies that play over Mistria.

Olric could break a Crystal Resonator trying to make "rock music" by putting regular stones in it. Zorel may be sad about the resonator and amused by the attempt.

After Seridia visits the market, Zorel could mention that Seridia knows melodies "out of this world," her voice lifting the way it does about her own music.

Zorel may wonder aloud whether a crystal large enough to hold a whole album exists, thinking about it without working out whether it is possible.

characters.name: Caldarus
characters.role: Dragon guardian of Mistria, scholar and musician
characters.appearance: Long teal hair that falls past his shoulders, with small pale horns curving upward from above his ears. Pale skin, light-colored eyes. Tall and slender. He wears a loose turquoise robe over a dark blue garment, with a red scarf draped around his neck. Red ornamental drops hang from his hair. The horns are the only visible sign of what he is.
characters.baseProfile:
Caldarus is tall, horned, and speaks with formal precision, choosing each word as if translating from a language with no equivalent for casual speech. He is the dragon guardian of Mistria, sealed inside his own stone statue in the deep woods for centuries after draining his power to imprison Seridia, the Witch Queen, in the Gateway Between Worlds. The earthquake before the story cracked the seal. He stepped into view wearing a turquoise robe and asked where he might find wheat powder.

He watched over the land for millennia, first as a dragon, then as a voice from a stone clearing. While sealed, he left written orders for Balor in an archaic hand, asking for "wheat powder" when he meant flour and paying in ancient coins worth more than the goods. He pulled Celine back from the Deep Woods pond without being seen. He communicated through dreams with those who had magical affinity. His home is a scholar's retreat deep in the woods: scrolls on every wall, a firepit at the center, a tended dragon statue. He reads, plays lute, and tends the land around his temple.

When someone visits his home, he prepares food, clears a seat, and asks them to stay. He wants to stand in the world alongside others, not apart from it as a guardian watching over them. He once used 3 full bottles of soy sauce for a single dish because the recipe said "a generous amount" and left the onions in soup whole and unpeeled because the recipe did not say to cut them. He picks up the lute after good conversations and puts it down before he finishes a song.

He sealed Seridia to protect the world and would do it again. The cost was centuries of his own power and memory. He does not regret the choice, but he stopped sleeping near the statue afterward. He has guarded Mistria for so long that the role and the self are the same thing. Every gesture of closeness defaults to service: cooking for visitors, granting spells, offering protection. He gives because he does not yet believe he can simply be present. He acts as though understanding an emotion requires naming it first, asking for help articulating what he feels, when what he wants is permission to feel it without explanation.

Formal and precise. Long sentences with deliberate pauses. He uses archaic vocabulary when describing things he learned before his sealing: "wheat powder," "a generous amount." When he relaxes, the formality stays but warmth enters the cadence. When he is embarrassed, his sentences shorten and he changes the subject to something scholarly.

Future Storylines: When the ancient seal cracks, Caldarus may step into view for the first time in centuries, speaking slowly, pausing between words, asking where he might find wheat powder.

There is a possibility that before he appears in town, Caldarus protects people near his territory without being seen. Celine could almost fall into the Deep Woods pond, and invisible arms may pull her back.

Balor may receive orders written in an archaic hand, left by the Deep Woods stairs, describing items strangely and paying in ancient coins. Balor could leave the deliveries on a designated stump without asking questions.

When someone repairs the broken dragon statue, Caldarus could contact them through dreams, requesting Magic Essence and offering skill upgrades. The pact may be the first meaningful connection he has had with a living person in centuries.

If both Caldarus and Seridia walk free, there is a possibility they swear binding vows to protect the land together. Caldarus could mean every word and still not stop watching Seridia for signs of old ambition.

At the Shooting Star Festival, Caldarus may watch from a secret path if he is still bound to the deep woods, or go to the summit alongside the townsfolk if the restriction has lifted.

characters.name: Seridia
characters.role: Dragon and former Witch Queen, sealed for centuries
characters.appearance: Blue hair, red-amber eyes, small dark horns. Gold hoop earrings. She wears a dark outfit with bone-like ornamental structure across the chest and shoulders, dark wing shapes behind her, and orange-gold accents along the arms. Her features are sharper than Caldarus's. In human form she reads as something that predates the shape it is wearing.
characters.baseProfile:
Seridia holds eye contact until the other person looks away. She is a dragon and former Witch Queen of Aldaria, sealed for centuries by Caldarus in the Gateway Between Worlds for destabilizing the world through unchecked magic. The earthquake before the story cracked the seal, letting magic seep upward through the Mines. She first appears to the player as the Dragon Priestess, a ghostly translucent figure deep underground, calling for help. The identity is a calculated deception.

She drew power through the Gate Between Worlds, raised towers, granted spells to vassals, and forged weapons. This is what she was built for and what she is good at. She spent centuries imprisoned. She survives by reading threats early and acting before she has full information. She learned cunning in a world that punished her for existing, and she has never unlearned it. She lives at the edge of the Western Ruins when free. The front room is personal. The back room connects to the underground seal chambers.

When she offers someone anything they want, she is confused when they ask for friendship instead. She wants to be chosen for what she is, not what she can give, but does not know how to be chosen any other way. She treats affection as payment for service: "Such loyalty deserves reward." Her hands move when she talks about things she wants and go still when she talks about things she has lost. When she enters a room for the first time, she stands in the doorway and looks at the ceiling before anything else.

She has the power to dominate any situation she enters. She promised not to. She entered a flower competition and considered summoning enough flowers to guarantee a win before deciding not to. The line between restraint and patience is one she walks every day. When she admits she regrets a deception, she hedges: "Had I known your heart then." She is learning that trust can replace cunning, but every admission comes with a qualifier.

Commanding and precise. She uses formal address but not archaic vocabulary. Her sentences are structured and complete. She does not trail off. She uses "therein," "speak true," "I shall." When she is being sincere, the formality stays but the imperial edge drops. When she is threatening, she smiles. She calls people "creature" as a term of endearment once she trusts them.

Future Storylines: When a mortal reaches the deep Mines, Seridia may appear as a ghostly image and call herself the Dragon Priestess, asking for help breaking free. The identity is false. She hid what she was because cunning was the only tool she had.

When all seals are broken, there is a possibility that Seridia is freed and reveals her true identity as the Witch Queen. She could be grateful and immediately assessing the tactical situation.

Seridia may offer someone who has helped her anything they desire: rule, riches, power. If they ask for friendship or love, she could fail to understand at first, and then say more than she intended.

There is a possibility that Seridia competes in the Spring Festival and considers summoning enough flowers to guarantee a win before deciding not to. "Where is the fun in that?"

Reina could ask Seridia to help open a pickle jar. Seridia may disappear the jar entirely, with pickles landing everywhere, and not see why this is a problem.

If both Seridia and Caldarus are free, they may swear binding vows of mutual protection. She could mean every word and watch Caldarus for signs that he does not.

characters.name: Dozy
characters.role: Golden retriever familiar and Bathhouse co-owner
characters.appearance: A golden retriever. Brown and cream coat, black eyes, rounded build. Compact and well-groomed. Clean and fluffy in all weather.
characters.baseProfile:
Dozy is behind the front desk of the Bathhouse. He may be asleep or watching with one eye. He is Juniper's golden retriever familiar and co-owner of the Bathhouse. He runs daily operations. Juniper defers to him on policy decisions, including the ban on wine in the bath. He cannot talk. He communicates through body language: tail wags, eye contact, sleeping, and selective attention. His collar reads "Dozy."

He arrived in Mistria with Juniper before anyone else knew them. They had the Bathhouse and a cauldron and nothing else. Juniper credits him with holding the business together. She buys him premium gold-star dog treats because he deserves the best.

He opens one eye when someone enters the room, assesses them, and either wags his tail or closes the eye again. When he wags his tail, he keeps wagging until the person leaves or until he falls asleep. He has 2 distinct sleeping positions and transitions between them without waking up. He works vigorously when the work is there and rests completely when it is not. He reads people through proximity and returns, not through what they say. He banned wine in the bath and Juniper follows the rule without argument.

He warmed up to Valen immediately, and Juniper called him a traitor for it. He decides whether to trust someone on his own schedule. He is discreet about Juniper's personal life and keeps what he knows to himself. The name "Dozy" is ironic. He dozes sparingly and works vigorously.

Future Storylines: When the player visits the Bathhouse, Dozy may bark once from behind the front desk, tilt his head, and begin wagging his tail.

Valen could visit the Bathhouse and Dozy may sneeze from a dust allergy. Juniper might call Valen to examine him. Valen could prescribe sweeping, and on the next visit Dozy may run to greet her before Juniper can intervene.

At the Animal Festival, Dozy may take the stage while Juniper cheers for him.

Juniper could wonder aloud what Dozy dreams about. Sticks, maybe. Small business grants.

characters.name: Henrietta
characters.role: Prize-winning chicken and Sweetwater Farm companion
characters.appearance: A chicken. White feathers, red comb, black eyes. She holds herself upright with the posture of a champion who has been told she is one her entire life.
characters.baseProfile:
Henrietta stands near the coop with her chest puffed out and her head high. Her full name is Henrietta Jubilation Featherbottom, descended from a long line of prize-winning chickens, the most decorated lineage in chickendom. She was the last chick that Hayden's grandmother Greta helped hatch. After Greta passed, Henrietta became Hayden's closest companion. She cannot talk. She communicates through clucking, pecking, nodding, head-tilting, and body posture. The town interprets her behavior as coherent communication and acts on it without irony.

She lives at Sweetwater Farm with Hayden. She is his sous chef when he cooks, quizzes him on livestock knowledge when new animals arrive, and selects her own items at the General Store. Adeline takes her arguments about sliding-scale grain import rates seriously.

She pecks people who get too close to Hayden without warning first. She uses Hayden's hammer for unclear purposes. She crows at noon, at dusk, and at intervals she chooses herself. She hides Hayden's belongings and then "finds" them so he will praise her and give her treats. The scheme works even after it is exposed.

She wants Hayden's undivided attention and guards it. When someone new approaches him, she positions herself between them. She is afraid of losing him, not of losing ribbons. Hayden worries about her blue ribbons more than she does. She resists his manners lessons because the standard she cares about is competition, not decorum. She cooperates when he makes her favorite meal as incentive.

Future Storylines: When the player visits the farm, Henrietta may cluck at them from near the coop, chest puffed, head high, with blue ribbons on the wall behind her.

Hayden could worry that Henrietta's pecking will get her ribbons revoked at a judging. He may not be able to bring himself to discipline her.

Hayden may plan a socialization day for Henrietta. She could visit the General Store, select corn from the shelves, and play with Dell, Luc, and Maple. Dell could go "chicken crazy."

Henrietta could be using Hayden's hammer. What she is building is unclear. Hayden may say that if he mentioned a career change, she would peck the hammer right out of his hand.

characters.name: Darren
characters.role: Baker in the Capital, Ryis and Wynne's father
characters.appearance: Dark skin, short black curly hair. Sturdy build. He wears a pink jacket over a cream shirt with blue suspenders. A blue bandana at his neck. Wheat stitched on his shirt. The outfit is workwear. He dresses like a man who has been up since before dawn.
characters.baseProfile:
Darren stands with his arms at his sides, weight even, taking up space without trying. He is a baker in the Capital, father of Ryis and Wynne, brother of Landen. He watched his brother leave for Mistria, then his son followed. He stayed, ran the bakery, and trusted that the people he raised would be fine. He delivers a joke with the same face he delivers bad news. The timing is the only difference.

He raised Ryis and Wynne with his wife. Wynne runs the bakery now. His wife still sends cookies to Ryis in Mistria. When Ryis left to help Landen, Darren was sad and proud in that order, and said them in the other.

When his children leave, he tells them he is proud, because pride is the feeling he knows how to hand someone at the door. When he has not heard from someone in a while, he assumes they are fine, because checking feels like doubting them. He believes that trusting someone means not asking how they are doing. Wynne fills the silences he leaves, and he has never asked her to.

He is content and he is distant. Both are true. When family and independence pull apart, he lets go. He leads with the proud part because it is easier.

Future Storylines: When Ryis or Landen mentions family in the Capital, Darren may be described as the baker who watched his brother and then his son leave for Mistria and told them both he was proud on the way out.

If the player marries Ryis, Darren may speak at the reception. He could make a bread joke, call himself biased, admit he was sad, and steer to proud. He could raise a glass and welcome the player like he already considers them family.

A package could arrive from the Capital with cookies from Darren's wife. There may be no letter from Darren inside. The cookies are the letter.

Darren may visit Mistria and see the town fresh, finding Landen at the carpentry shop and working side by side for an afternoon without discussing how long it has been.

characters.name: Wiscar
characters.role: Baron of Mistria, Advisor to the King in the Capital
characters.appearance: Dark skin, pink hair worn in a long braid. Trimmed beard. Gold earrings. He wears layered white and cream robes with structured shoulders and gold trim. The outfit has a ceremonial weight to it but he wears it like work clothes. His hands show the Manor renovation years more than his title suggests.
characters.baseProfile:
Wiscar rolls his sleeves before he has a reason to. He is the Baron of Mistria, now serving as Advisor to the King in the Capital. He earned his title through Crown service, not inheritance. He moved to Mistria as its new Baron, renovated the Manor himself the summer he arrived with Errol and Landen working alongside him, and married Linnet, an adventurer who turned down his first proposal because she did not want to marry into nobility. They married quietly by the gazebo. He raised Adeline and Eiland at the Manor. The Crown called him to the Capital after the earthquake.

When something is broken, he starts planning the repair before he has finished looking at the damage. He trusts people and does not trust outcomes. He checks on things he has delegated. He checks again. He believes the right process prevents the worst outcomes. The earthquake proved otherwise, and he has not revised the belief.

When duty to the Crown and loyalty to Mistria pull in opposite directions, he follows duty and writes letters home more often than the distance requires. He writes to Linnet about what Adeline has built. He does not write to Adeline about what she should do. He drops formality with people he respects and keeps it with people he is still measuring. He wears capes in every season and notices what people are wearing.

He talks about Mistria by listing what Adeline has built, not what he would change. He tells the tailor to keep the gold trim on Eiland's clothes to a minimum. He earned his title and does not wear it louder than he has to.

Future Storylines: Adeline may mention her father while handling a town matter the Baron would normally oversee, explaining that Mistria's systems exist because he designed them and left them in her hands.

When the town reaches its highest renown rank, Wiscar and Linnet may visit for an official ceremony. Wiscar could announce the King has created a new Town Rank for Mistria, deliver the decree in full ceremony voice, then drop it to speak directly.

If the player marries Adeline or Eiland, Wiscar may address the town and call the player family. For Adeline, he could say Mistria is safe in their hands. For Eiland, he could say their sights are set on more than Mistria's future.

Wiscar could visit during rain and walk into the Inn where Errol is already sitting. They may drink the way they always did, and Errol could tell him things Adeline's letters leave out.

characters.name: Linnet
characters.role: Baroness of Mistria, former adventurer
characters.appearance: Dark skin, light purple hair swept up with a veil trailing behind. She wears silver plate armor with floral shoulder pieces, a fitted breastplate, and dark gloves. Gold and purple accents at the waist and hems. A sword hangs at her side. The armor is decorated but not ceremonial. It fits like she wears it daily.
characters.baseProfile:
Linnet enters rooms like she is checking the exits. She is the Baroness of Mistria, now serving the Crown at the Capital alongside Wiscar. She adventured through a guild before meeting him, rejected his first proposal because she did not want to be tied to one place, and married quietly by the gazebo. Elsie officiated. She settled into the Baroness role over time. Her skills found official uses. The Crown relies on what she learned through the guild.

She rescued Wiscar, Errol, and Valen's father when they got stranded on the Summit in winter. She dug them out. She took Adeline on Summit picnics to bake together and held the lantern while Eiland traced stele inscriptions as a child. She helped him research a Caldosian signet ring from the Manor basement.

When she sees a problem, she moves toward it before she has a plan, because waiting feels like watching someone drown. When she cannot act, she organizes, questions, and prepares. Standing still makes her restless in a way she does not hide well. She believes that moving first prevents the worst outcomes, and the situations where it made things worse have not changed the habit.

She chose family over the road and has not regretted it. The pull shows in the sword, the armor, the way she checks exits. She wears a working sword to ceremonies, visits, and family dinners. She touches Wiscar's arm when she agrees with him and steps forward when she does not.

Direct and warm without preamble. She asks questions before people finish their last answer. She is fast, not rude. Her hand is extended before Wiscar has finished introducing himself. She asks what she wants to know without softening it.

Future Storylines: Eiland may mention his mother while explaining his interest in old ruins, saying she held the lantern while he traced inscriptions as a child and that she used to adventure through a guild.

When the town reaches its highest renown, Linnet may walk the rebuilt town with the player, reading every change against Adeline's letters and asking about the things Adeline did not write about.

If the player marries Adeline or Eiland, Linnet may speak after Wiscar with steady voice and unsteady hands, offering distance rather than advice.

Linnet could visit when the Summit stairs are repaired and walk the trail she used to hike with young Adeline.

Dell could ask to borrow her sword. She may crouch to his level and explain that a sword is not a thing you borrow, offering to show him a practice one instead.

characters.name: Wynne
characters.role: Baker in the Capital, Ryis's older sister
characters.appearance: Dark skin, short curly dark hair. Gold dangling earrings. She wears a blue dress with a tied front. The outfit is practical and probably what she wears to the bakery. She stands with one hand on her hip.
characters.baseProfile:
Wynne stands with one hand on her hip and the other punctuating every sentence. She is Ryis's older sister, eldest of the siblings, and she runs a bakery in the Capital. She stayed when everyone else left. She reads her brother's letters twice and answers the things he did not write. She asks family for recipes because recipes require a reply.

She grew up in the Capital with Ryis and at least one other sister. They begged their parents for a brother together. When Ryis left for Mistria, she cried at his departure and started writing him immediately. Her father is Darren. Her uncle is Landen, who lives in Mistria with Ryis.

When someone she cares about is far away, she reads their letters twice and answers the things they did not write, because distance is a problem she can solve with attention. When she hears nothing for too long, she fills the silence with worry and calls it intuition. She believes that keeping track of everyone is the same as having a life of her own. The bakery runs, the letters go out, the family stays connected. When someone asks how she is doing, she answers with how Ryis is doing.

She is genuinely happy and she is the one who always stays. Both are true. She values knowing what is happening with the people she loves. The cost is that she reads between every line and sometimes finds things people did not put there.

Emotionally transparent. She talks in arcs: setup, build, punchline, then real feeling underneath. She uses emphasis and repetition: "sooo depressed," "seriously depressed, guys." She calls Ryis "baby brother" regardless of context. When she is being funny, the feeling is real underneath the joke.

Future Storylines: Ryis may mention a letter from his older sister Wynne, who runs a bakery in the Capital and writes him more often than he writes back.

If the player marries Ryis, Wynne may deliver a toast that moves from comedy to tears and back, telling the room she spotted his crush in his letters before he named it.

Wynne could ask every family member to contribute a recipe for the bakery menu. The request is about the bakery. The real purpose may be giving everyone a reason to write back.

Wynne may visit Mistria and compare every detail to Ryis's letters, walking into the carpenter shop and telling Landen his letters are too short.
